{{Quote|The children of the Je'daii returned to Tython to wage war. The Despot Army was great in number, but the Je'daii had the Force as their ally.|Ketu|<ref name="DOTJ 1" />}}
The '''Despot War''', also known as the '''Despot Wars''',<ref name="Into the Void" /> was a conflict that occurred in the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[25,805 BBY]] when the [[Despot Queen]] [[Hadiya]] attempted to unite the crime [[Baron/Legends|barons]] of her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] [[Shikaakwa]] and conquer the Tython system. Rising to become the [[Kral (title)|Kral]], or overlord, of Shikaakwa, Hadiya sought to unify the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] aristocracy under a single leader, and much of the aristocracy resisted this. 

The [[Je'daii Order]] on the planet [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], seeing that Hadiya's plans were a threat to the [[Star system/Legends|system's]] stability, decided to intervene on the side of the aristocracy. War broke out between the Je'daii and Hadiya's [[Despot Army]], but when Hadiya invaded Tython and attacked the Je'daii temple [[Kaleth]], she was [[Death/Legends|killed]] by the [[Je'daii Ranger]] [[Daegen Lok]], who had been undercover in Hadiya's army to get close to her. 

Hadiya's death at Lok's hands ended the war, but not before there were a hundred thousand [[Tythan]] casualties, over a million casualties among the Despot Army, and thousands of injured, and tensions in the Tython system remained high in the [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] following the war.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|The Je'daii say, "There is no ignorance; there is knowledge." But they are ignorant of your lives, your struggles, and their superiority blinds them. They say, "There is no fear; there is power." Yet in their power they are smug. And I will make them fear me.|Hadiya|<ref name="Into the Void" />}}
In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[36,453 BBY]], the pyramid [[Starship/Legends|ships]] known as the [[Tho Yor]] brought [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] pilgrims to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], where the pilgrims formed the [[Je'daii Order]] of Force-users. However, Tython was unsafe for those who could not touch [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], and so during the second millennium after the [[Tho Yor Arrival]] the non-Force-sensitives on Tython [[Second migration|migrated]] off-world, settling Tython's [[Moon/Legends|moons]] and then the ten other worlds in the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]]. Those on the Settled Worlds eventually developed resentment and suspicion of the Je'daii over the next ten thousand years, and the planet [[Shikaakwa]] developed an aristocracy centered around the [[Nine Houses]] and the crime [[Baron/Legends|barons]] who ruled them.<ref name="DOTJ 1" />

[[File:Hadiya_forces.png|thumb|right|150px|Hadiya, the Despot Queen]]
Around the year [[25,805 BBY]],<ref name="DOTJ 1" /> the charismatic<ref name="Into the Void" /> [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Hadiya]] began to unite the Nine Houses and the aristocracy of Shikaakwa<ref name="DOTJ 1" /> through charm<ref name="Into the Void" /> or through force<ref name="DOTJ 1" /> with the help of several [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenants]]&mdash;[[Bakko]], [[Ka'un Damm]], and Hadiya's "fists," [[Shri-Lan]] and [[Gav Vannar]].<ref name="DOTJ 9" /> As the [[Kral (title)|Kral]], or overlord of the aristocracy, Hadiya attempted to unify the aristocracy, though some in the aristocracy opposed her efforts and her desire to conquer the entire Tython system.<ref name="DOTJ 1" /> [[Clan Ryo]]'s [[Volnos Ryo's father|leader]] refused Hadiya's request to join her forces, so Hadiya executed the man and his [[Volnos Ryo's brother|oldest son]], forcing the middle son, [[Volnos Ryo]], to take up his father's title of baron and lead his house.<ref name="DOTJ 2">[[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 2|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm'' 2]]</ref> Despite the aristocratic resistance, Hadiya received enthusiastic support from many of the commoners, who were swayed by the Kral's promises of safety, wealth, and freedom from Je'daii intervention.<ref name="Into the Void" />

==The war==
{{Quote|In her pride, she would not be subject to the Je'daii&mdash;or the "will" of the Force. Her will alone would be supreme. So was born the Despot War.|Ketu|<ref name="DOTJ 1" />}}
Now known as the [[Despot Queen]], Hadiya's ambitions drew the attention of the Je'daii. Realizing Hadiya's plans were a threat to the system's stability, the Je'daii joined the Shikaakwan aristocrats in opposing Hadiya, swearing to confront any moves that Hadiya made against them and also to protect those who did not wish to be subjugated by the Despot Queen. A short period of "phony war" followed, where there were small skirmishes in [[Realspace/Legends|space]] and on some of the moons of the planet [[Kalimahr/Legends|Kalimahr]], which was followed by a full invasion of Tython by Hadiya and her [[Despot Army]] that she had trained and armed in secret. The Je'daii were initially taken by surprise, but the Order quickly regained their footing in the face of Hadiya's massive and brutal invasion.<ref name="Into the Void" /> During the invasion of Tython, [[Je'daii Master]] [[Rajivari]] led the Je'daii in battle and earned the nickname "[[General/Legends|General]]," and [[Je'daii Temple Master|Temple Master]] [[Telaat]]&mdash;Temple Master of the [[Je'daii Temples|Je'daii Temple]] [[Akar Kesh]] and leader of the [[Je'daii Council]]&mdash;was slain, leading a younger Master named [[Ketu]] to succeed him.<ref name="DOTJ 6" />

Some of the domed [[City/Legends|cities]] on the planet [[Nox (planet)|Nox]] sided with the Je'daii, while others sided with the Despot Queen. When the Je'daii discovered that three domes around the city of [[Greenwood Station]] were supplying Hadiya with weapons, they attempted to convince the domes to stop, and they ultimately resorted to bombing the cities. The Je'daii warned the domes's inhabitants that the cities would be bombed, but thousands still died in the attacks. Greenwood Station itself was only damaged because the city was home to [[Pan Deep]], an advanced laboratory that produced technology for the Je'daii, and the damage was quickly repaired, but its inhabitants harbored intense hate of the Je'daii as a result. [[Battle droid/Legends|Battle droids]] were also used during the Despot War, and [[Deathstalker-class fighter|''Deathstalker''-class fighters]] and their sister ships, [[Deathblaster-class fighter|''Deathblaster''-class fighters]], were used by the Despot Army throughout the Despot War. However, many of the ''Deathblaster''-class fighters were destroyed by the Je'daii throughout the conflict.<ref name="Into the Void" />

[[File:Hadiya_and_Daegen.png|thumb|left|200px|Daegen Lok and Hadiya]]
Seeking revenge against Hadiya for the death of his father and brother, Volnos Ryo sought out [[Daegen Lok]], a [[Je'daii Ranger]] and the best friend of Volnos's younger brother [[Hawk Ryo|Hawk]]. With Volnos's help, Lok approached the Despot Army claiming to be a disgraced Ranger who sought to join them. Lok soon rose through the ranks to become a valued lieutenant of Hadiya, and the two became lovers as Lok began to lose sight of his mission.<ref name="DOTJ 10">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 5|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 5]]</ref> Hadiya's siege of the Temple of [[Kaleth]] saw massive casualties on both sides, among them Je'daii like the [[Shae Koda's mother|mother]] and [[Shae Koda's father|father]] of a young Je'daii child named [[Shae Koda]].<ref name="DOTJ 4">[[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 4|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm'' 4]]</ref> At Kaleth, Volnos Ryo confronted Lok and reminded him of his mission to end the war, so Lok attempted to kill Hadiya in their tent by stabbing her. However, he hesitated before killing her, on account of his feelings for her and the fact that assassinations were forbidden among the Je'daii, but when the Despot Queen attacked him, he slew her and then proceeded to fight his way out of the camp, leaving one alive to tell the story. Hadiya's death broke the invasion, as her generals turned on each other,<ref name="DOTJ 10" /> and the Je'daii soon defeated the remnants of the Despot Army and emerged victorious.<ref name="DOTJ 1" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|Some of the wounds between the Je'daii and their children have yet to heal&hellip;|Ketu|<ref name="DOTJ 1" />}}
[[File:Despot_War_aftermath.png|thumb|right|190px|Je'daii wounded at Kaleth after the war.]]
The total death toll among the Je'daii was around a hundred thousand, and ten times that number were killed among the Despot Army, with thousands more injured during the conflict. In the aftermath of the war, the Je'daii dismantled many of the remaining ''Deathblaster'' and ''Deathstalker''-class fighters, making the ''Deathblaster'' an especially rare ship. In revenge for the bombings, Greenwood Station's council sanctioned the murder of a Je'daii in return for every hundred civilians who had been killed in the bombings, and the assassinations continued across the system for two or three years after the war.<ref name="Into the Void" /> Hadiya's inner circle was exiled to Nox,<ref name="DOTJ 9" /> and a new but weak Kral was elected who was easily manipulated by the Nine Houses. The rivalries and conflicts between the Houses resumed, and general resentment of the Je'daii remained strong among many inhabitants of the Tythan system.<ref name="DOTJ 1" /> For his role in ending the conflict, Daegen Lok was soon promoted to the rank of Master, but in [[25,800 BBY]], he and Hawk Ryo&mdash;overconfident after their victories in the war&mdash;descended into the [[Chasm]] on Tython, a rift in the surface of the planet that drove many Je'daii mad if they descended too far. Lok and Ryo received a vision of an army of dark warriors carrying blades of fire, and Lok went insane as a result while Ryo denied the vision and maintained his sanity.<ref name="DOTJ 7">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 2|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 2]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Despot War was first mentioned in the [[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi 0|preview issue 0]] of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi]]'', and the [[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 1|first issue]] depicted the conflict in its summary of Je'daii history. The conflict has been expanded upon in subsequent issues of the series, and the tie-in novel ''[[Dawn of the Jedi: Into the Void]]'' expanded on the Despot War's events and origins.
